title: Willie Smith and Harry James's mixed band
summary: Willard tells how Willie Smith, who looks white, passed in Harry James's band and was a convenience when food was hard to get.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I know Willie used to tell stories about when he was with Harry James, and how they would -- advance word would get to these other cities that Harry James had a mixed band. There was one Negro in the band. And so, the sheriff would come up and say to Harry James you can't go on with a mixed band. And Harry would say, all right, point out the one that mixes it.

Who could tell looking at Willie. And so -- and other times Harry James would be told he couldn't go on if he let Willie play. And so, Harry James would walk away and not play the date. But on the other hand, it was a convenience when you couldn't get food.
